description: The bar chart, titled "Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning Design Spaces," displays five distinct distribution patterns—labeled 'Increasing,' 'Uniform,' 'Decreasing,' 'Spindle,' and 'Bottleneck'—along the horizontal axis, with the vertical axis representing the relative values of each distribution. In the 'Increasing' pattern, bar heights progressively rise from left to right, showing a consistent upward trend. The 'Decreasing' pattern demonstrates the opposite, with bar heights gradually diminishing from left to right. The 'Uniform' distribution features bars of approximately equal height across all categories, indicating no variation. The 'Spindle' distribution exhibits a symmetric pattern, with the tallest bars concentrated in the center and tapering off toward the edges. In contrast, the 'Bottleneck' distribution has the shortest bars at the center, with the outermost bars being approximately 50% taller than the central ones. Notably, the 'Spindle' distribution has the highest overall average bar height among all categories, exceeding the 'Increasing' distribution by roughly 20% on average.
